expected: A session's injection follows the context that session bound (via its own session record or a marker attributable to it), never another session's newer bind. If the session cannot be attributed to any bind, fall back to generic preflight, not to another session's context memory.
notes: Found live during the 2026-07-01 full workspace audit while bound in read mode. Suggested direction: key injection to the session's own bind (session record self-keyed via harness sid, or marker files carrying the minted sid cross-referenced through the by-session index), and never select a marker purely by global recency. Re-binding as a workaround is symmetric poison: it steals the other session's injection back.
repro: Session 1: dadaia context bind ctx-a, exchange one prompt (sentinel stamped). Session 2 (separate harness session): dadaia context bind ctx-b. Back in session 1, submit any prompt: the injected '=== workspace memory ===' block is ctx-b's tech-stack + catalog.
symptom: A session bound to context A received context B's full memory bootstrap (tech-stack digest + catalog) on its next prompt. Observed live: session bound context A (marker written 16:52 local), a second concurrent session bound context B at 17:15; on the first session's next UserPromptSubmit the hook injected context B's memory. Root cause: the bind-driven injection step selects the newest bind-epoch marker newer than this session's sentinel across ALL contexts — markers carry a slug but no session affinity, so with concurrent sessions in different contexts the most recent bind wins for every session whose sentinel is older. The flagship parallel-multi-project scenario is exactly the one that breaks; the wrong project's memory can steer wrong-project writes.
title: ctx-inject injects the wrong context: newest bind-epoch marker globally wins, so a concurrent session's bind steals another session's memory injection
